matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides (including any addition or subtraction) before moving any stick, to know the numeric imbalance that must be corrected.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick equation, before any stick is moved.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick without first checking the numeric difference, leading to an equation that remains false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly +5 and a V appears on the side that needs to increase, move one diagonal stick from that V to turn it into an X, raising that side’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When imbalance = +5 and a V is present on the side that must increase.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V when the imbalance is not +5, causing an incorrect value change.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already contains at least one I to another numeral that needs an extra I, increasing the destination by 1 and decreasing the source by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is even and an I can be transferred without invalidating the source numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing an I from a numeral that only has one I, leaving an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Reposition I relative to V to change IV↔VI
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains IV (or VI) and the numeric imbalance is 2, move the I‑stick from before the V to after the V (or vice‑versa) to change IV↔VI, adjusting the value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When imbalance = 2 and IV or VI appears.
matchstick.example: Moving the I in IV to create an invalid numeral like IIV.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly –5 and an X appears on the side that must decrease, move one of the diagonal sticks from that X to turn it into a V, lowering that side’s value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When imbalance = –5 and X is present on the side to decrease.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the minus into an equals and the equals into a minus, thereby swapping their functions.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When both '-' and '=' appear and swapping them could resolve the numeric imbalance.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=', leaving only one horizontal and breaking the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is on the side that exceeds the other side by exactly +3 (RHS larger by 3) and there is an I (or space for a new I) on either side, moving the plus’s vertical stick to that I (or to create a new I) turns ‘+’ into ‘-’ and changes the numeric values by 3, balancing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is on the side that has excess value of 3 and an I can receive the vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' without adding it to an I, leaving the equation still unbalanced or creating an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick from the equality sign, ensure that at least one horizontal stick remains so that the ‘=’ sign stays valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a stick from '='.
matchstick.example: Moving both horizontals from '=', eliminating the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI↔IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains the pattern ‘XI’, moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes it to ‘IX’, adjusting the value by 2.
matchstick.example: Moving the I in XI to a position that creates an invalid numeral like IIX.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality when imbalance is 2
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 2, you can move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on one side to a numeral on the other side, decreasing the source by 1 and increasing the destination by 1, thereby balancing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When imbalance = 2 and an I can be transferred across the equality without invalidating the source.
matchstick.example: Transferring an I from a solitary I, leaving an invalid numeral on the source side.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any numeral can give up a stick without checking whether the remaining strokes still form a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before removing a stick, verify that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after the removal.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick‑movement step and neglects to ensure the resulting equation is syntactically and semantically complete.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After the transformation, check that all symbols are valid Roman numerals or operators and that the equation is well‑formed.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid ‘=’ sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: When relocating a horizontal from '=', the model may inadvertently remove both horizontals, destroying the equality operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick from '=', always keep at least one horizontal stick so that ‘=’ remains recognizable.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after achieving a visually correct arrangement without recomputing the arithmetic result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate both sides of the equation after the move and confirm that the numeric values are equal.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes thinks multiple adjustments are needed to fix the equation and performs them together.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce a strict count of exactly one stick moved and track the source and destination of that single stick.
